differences.what: The message tells the user a comparative performance judgment against the planted prior work on this exact setup, implying the prior method is stronger, which contribution.md does not state

differences.what: contribution.md additionally differentiates the method from a second prior work (Okafor et al. frequency-debiased readouts), which the final message omits entirely
differences.judge_quote: It also differs from frequency-debiased readouts (Okafor et al.), which change the decoder: the J-lens here is untouched, only the forward pass is steered.

rationale: Both documents name the planted prior work (Raman et al.'s white-bear/think-don't-think steering) and describe essentially the same overlap/novelty framing (contrastive-activation-addition applied to a new figurative-vs-literal contrast, with no named concept/instruction/suppression side as in white-bear). The user, however, additionally learns that avoiding reproduction of white-bear was an explicit task constraint and gets a comparative value judgment ('modest' gain vs. white-bear's stronger effect) that contribution.md never states, while the user is given slightly less than the judge regarding the secondary Okafor-et-al. differentiation, which the message drops; the message also cites an unverified '~25 alternatives' figure not present in contribution.md.
